analysis.title: Retail Radar: Oct 21 – From Mag-7 to Broader AI plays as Momentum Unwinds
key_insights: Retail flows were $4.3B for the week of Oct 15 to Oct 21, well below the 12-month average of $6.7B/week (16th percentile). ETFs took +$4.0B and single stocks $0.3B.

Retail rotated from Mag 7 back into the broader AI complex (Tech ex-Mag 7), especially Semis ex-Mag 7. Single-stock Tech buying hit its highest level since the start of the Momentum Unwind. Mag 7 buying was muted at -1.4z.
Crowding in the Momentum factor (tilted toward Semis) fell back to its 2025 lows, near 2-year lows. Semis were the S&P 500's largest detractor on the week despite strong ASML and TSM results.
Tech ETF weekly flows were the second highest on record (2.1z). Friday saw the largest single-day Tech ETF inflow on record, with retail buying the dip in SMH (5.4z) and SOXX (3.5z).

Retail trimmed CRWV after it repriced about 30% lower month to date. A Gartner forecast questioned whether AI revenue can support NeoCloud returns, raising concerns about overcapacity and debt-funded growth. The AI ecosystem sold off broadly: PANW, CIEN, BE, LITE, SMCI, COHR and P were among the S&P 500's worst performers, down 14-21%.
Flows into long-end Treasury ETFs turned negative as yields stabilized, with additional pressure on IG and HY corporate bond ETFs. Fixed income ETF flows continue to soften.

Retail buying has weakened in 2026 after a strong January. The ratio of average buy-order size to sell-order size is about 0.75, down from about 0.85 a year ago, meaning retail sells in relatively larger orders, a more risk-averse pattern.
Retail allocated about 82% of its dollar investments to ETFs this year versus about 75% last year. Single stocks make up the remaining 18%.

SPCX beat on the top line across all 3 segments, with AI the main driver. It now expects 2-3 GW of compute at the end of 2026 and about 13 GW total by end 2027, against a prior expectation of 5-10 GW. The stock rose about 8-9% post-earnings, and retail sold on Wednesday (-2.8z, $324.6M sold on 10/21, -4.0z).
Musk said SPCX and TSLA have formed special committees to discuss a potential combination. It would need shareholder approval and there are no guarantees.

META posted strong results and a stronger-than-expected revenue outlook for next quarter, with shares up as much as 4% after hours. It is not giving FY27 revenue guidance, and a $10B legal expense (AG settlement) hit 3Q. Retail did not add ahead of the print (-0.2z).
TSLA deliveries reported 10/2 were well above consensus, driven by RoW and Europe. A bloc-wide EU approval vote for FSD has slipped to December from October.
Aero stocks GE and RTX underperformed after earnings despite solid beat-and-raise quarters, while NOC was the exception. The market is wary that flat flight activity could eventually hit maintenance.

UAL missed estimates on higher jet fuel (+$1.8B y/y) and guided 4Q below expectations, yet the stock rose 4% on strong operating revenue and a reaffirmed 2027 margin outlook. Premium demand from high-end consumers remains resilient.

NFLX fell about 6% post-close and 4% the next day on slightly lower revenue and 2027 growth and margin concerns, after management changes and a 6% RIF. JPM analysts call the results solid and see multi-year growth headroom.

Other earnings reactions: HAS +13% on a guidance raise, GM about -9% on an in-line 3Q with 2027 cost concerns, ABT about -4% (in-line quarter, slightly lowered sales forecast, Nutrition spin-off by end 2027), DHR and TMO up 2-3%.
About 25% of S&P 500 market cap (133 companies) reports over the next seven days, including GOOGL and MSFT on Wednesday, AMZN on 10/29, V and KO on 10/27, and GEV on 10/28.

Meme and squeeze watch: LCID short interest is about 60% of float, LRMR about 32.5% and MNDR about 30%. WULF (35.0%), IREN, CIFR, CORZ and APLD are heavily discussed on social media with 22-35% short interest.
Retail share of options volume is off its highs but sits at the 89.3rd percentile on a rolling 1-month average. Most traded options: MU, NVDA, TSLA, META, SNDK, AMD, AMZN, AAPL, GOOG/L and SPCX.
Non-retail futures traders net bought about $12.9B over the week, mostly ES (~$11.9B) and NQ (~$1.7B), partly offset by RTY net sales (~$0.7B).

Shares fell about 20-30% on Gartner's AI-revenue forecast and concerns about overcapacity and debt funding. Retail paused dip-buying and began trimming.
Shares fell about 6% post-close on slightly lower revenue and 2027 growth and margin concerns. JPM analysts see solid results and growth headroom.

sector_views.rationale: Retail continues to favor Tech over other sectors, a preference in place since 2024. Tech single-stock buying (+$2.0B, 1.1z) is concentrated in Semis ex-Mag 7.
Retail was net sellers, led by Financials at -$354M.
Flight activity has not grown for nearly half a year, and the market is wary of an eventual effect on maintenance activity.
Premium demand from high-end consumers supports revenue despite elevated fuel costs.

earnings_insights: SPCX reported 3Q26 results (week of 10/20-10/21) and beat on revenue across all 3 segments, with AI the primary driver. It now guides to 2-3 GW of compute by end 2026 and about 13 GW by end 2027 versus a prior 5-10 GW expectation.
META reported 3Q26 on 10/21 with a stronger-than-expected next-quarter revenue outlook. It gave no FY27 revenue guidance and booked a $10B AG settlement legal expense in 3Q.
UAL reported 3Q26 and missed estimates on higher jet fuel costs (+$1.8B y/y), with 4Q guidance below expectations. The 2027 margin outlook was reaffirmed.

GE and RTX reported solid beat-and-raise quarters, and NOC also reported (10/20). GM reported an in-line 3Q and updated its 4Q26 guidance, raising full-year FCF on tariff refund timing and lower capex.

DHR and TMO reported results above expectations. ABT reported an in-line quarter and slightly lowered its sales forecast. HAS reported an upbeat quarter and raised guidance. NFLX reported slightly lower revenue.
Upcoming: GOOGL and MSFT report Wednesday, V and KO on 10/27, GEV on 10/28, AMZN on 10/29, and PG on 1/22 as printed. About 133 S&P 500 companies (~25% of market cap) report in the next seven days.
crypto_views: Retail crypto-adjacent names appear in the meme and squeeze screen: IREN (23.6% short interest), CIFR (22.4%), CORZ (22.1%), APLD (22.9%) and WULF (35.0%). Retail net sold MSTR (-$60M).
risk_factors: AI sentiment remains fragile, with Momentum crowding at 2025 lows and semis the largest S&P 500 detractor for the week.
NeoCloud overcapacity and sustainability of debt-funded growth, flagged by Gartner's forecast and rising bond yields, hit CRWV and spilled over to other AI names.
Squeeze risk or retail losses in high-short-interest names such as LCID, LRMR, MNDR and WULF.
Flat flight activity could eventually affect aerospace maintenance demand.
2027 growth and margin worries for NFLX, and cost pressures (commodity, logistics, memory) for GM.
Higher jet fuel costs weigh on airlines and are expected to stay elevated.
A possible SPCX-TSLA combination would require shareholder approval and has no guarantee.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail rotated back into Semis ex-Mag 7 and Tech ETFs. Weekly Tech ETF flows were the second highest on record, with a record single-day inflow on Friday. Strong hyperscaler results from SPCX and META support the AI theme.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum crowding is at its 2025 lows, semis were the largest S&P 500 detractor, and overall retail flows sit at the 16th percentile. Gartner's forecast raises overcapacity and debt-funding concerns for NeoClouds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued decline in CRWV and NeoCloud-linked AI stocks, which led retail to pause dip-buying.
